title: Clear dry leaves from a gutter
instruction: Scoop the leaves out of the gutter into the blue bucket. Leave the gutter clear and the bucket upright.
context: A gutter scoop must pass beneath the roof overhang and work inside the curved channel without scattering the debris.
setup: A 600 mm length of 112 mm half-round PVC gutter is secured to a timber fascia on a 747.5 mm-high table. Its rim is 140 mm above the table; a roof edge overhangs the opening by 16 mm and a bracket crosses it 220 mm from the centre. Twelve loose, dry, intact leaves (about 60 × 26 mm, 0.3 g each) lie in the channel. A plastic gutter scoop has a 90 × 110 mm curved bowl and a 140 mm hollow handle raised 70 mm above its floor. An empty blue plastic bucket has a 170 mm inner diameter and is 150 mm high. Gutter centre: (300, 0) mm; scoop: (180, 20) mm; bucket: (360, −400) mm. The setup image and geometry specify leaf placement. No leaves are glued or attached.
scoring: After both hands release for one second, score the number of whole leaves entirely inside the bucket divided by 12. The bucket must stay within 40 mm of its starting centre and within 18.2° of upright. Any leaf falling off the work surface or broken equipment makes the score zero. Leaves remaining in the gutter, scoop or on the table earn no credit. Other outcomes score zero. Count leaves from the final views and use a ruler for bucket displacement.
fidelity: Dry leaves are passive articulated strips with contact and bending. No wet adhesion or brittle fragmentation is modelled. The roof section is full size and lowered to a bench-safe height, preserving overhang and bracket access. Native contacts move the scoop and leaves.
scores: Development only: not validated; do not submit.
reset_notes: Use twelve dry leaves of similar dimensions, without wet adhesion. Empty the bucket, inspect for tears, replace damaged leaves, and restore the pictured layout. The secured roof section is reusable. The setup represents local gutter cleaning at bench height; it does not test ladder use or working at height.
